cells.tense: Right now you are naming the shape of a thing and it holds because you said it plainly.
cells.act: let several things be true and act on one
cells.ask: When two readings both fit, keep both and act on the clearer one before the day ends.
cells.core:
Right now you can say how something is shaped while you're still inside it, and it lands. Not a theory you'll test later — the shape as it is, declared, and people around it get steadier. Things make sense once you've put them into words. Part of why that works is that you don't need the whole picture first.

You can hold more than one reading of a thing at once and stay easy there. So when two answers are true, keep both in view and act on the one that's clearest, without pretending the other went away. The rest keep. You don't have to pick between them to move.
cells.sheetLine: You declare the shape and it holds.
cells.verb: declaring the shape of a thing so it holds
cells.place: where the pattern shows itself with nothing in it

cells.tense: You are about to force the whole framework onto people tonight before you have met its edge.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Take a pattern you're pressing on people and follow it in your own thinking until it runs out. Then stop.
cells.core:
There's a framework taking shape and an urge to hand it over whole — names, rules, the full architecture — before you've walked to the end of it yourself. It reaches the room before you do. You're organizing aloud to stay on top of something that hasn't settled, so the plan keeps getting firmer while the ground under it doesn't.

Holding the framework back isn't the move. Going further into it than you're comfortable going, alone, is: find the place it gives — the case that doesn't fit, the part you can't yet say. Sit there a minute instead of surfacing. Build outward from that edge after. What you hand over then is reliable, because you already found where it fails.

cells.tense: You put the shape of something into words once and you are still at that closed door.
cells.act: commit to the long build and do today's part
cells.ask: Go back to the build behind the claim you stopped making. Do today's small concrete piece of it, in one sitting, then stop.
cells.core:
You saw the shape of something and said so once, and you haven't said it again since. The claim is where you left it. Seeing patterns comes easily to you; saying them does not, and here you wait to be certain before you speak, which isn't how certainty arrives.

What's empty is the charge, not the sight. So don't push feeling into the pattern. Charge the other channel: return to the build behind the claim and do today's real piece of it. One page, one draft, one finished cut, done the same way tomorrow. The structure under this comes back by being worked, and the claim comes back with it — not by reasoning harder, but by returning to the work.

cells.tense: While you say you aren't holding the line, you are the one drawing it for everyone else.
cells.ask: Pick a decision you made that shaped other people, put it on paper in your own hand, and sign your name.
cells.core:
Somewhere you decided — what a project can attempt, who works together, how a shared thing is actually run — and it quietly held because you set the shape of it. If someone asked, you'd say it worked out by itself. There's no seam in that shape, which is why it's stayed so easy to leave unnoticed.

Here's the smaller, plainer move. Pick one call you've made for other people and said nothing about. Put it on paper, in your own hand: 'I decided this.' Not to ask permission — you already made it — but to stand beside it. Then what you do next has a name on it. And next time you shape a thing, you'll know it's you doing the shaping.
cells.sheetLine: The shape holds quietly because you set it.
cells.verb: declaring the shape of a thing so it holds
